_readme: Upcoming English-language Pokemon TCG releases, plus a separately labeled
Japanese calendar. Hand maintained: there is no API for things that have not
happened yet.
confidence is one of:
confirmed  an official date from The Pokemon Company or Pokemon Center
window     an official month or quarter, but no exact day
expected   a product lineup that matches every previous set in the series
but which TPCi has not announced. Retailer preorder pages often
list these; they are templated from the last set, not sourced.
There are three of them and there are deliberately not four. A product that
has been SHOWN in official artwork but given no date and no price of its own
is not any of the three, and the answer is a sentence in productNote saying
exactly that, not a fourth badge: data/drops.json's own readme says it uses
'the same three words as data/upcoming.json', so a fourth word here quietly
makes that file wrong. Leave such a product's confidence unset, which is this
file's existing way of saying 'as well known as the set it is in'.
RULES FOR EDITING THIS FILE
Never add a set that has not been officially named. Several AI-written card
sites invent them, and one of them called Chaos Rising 'Rising Chaos'.
Never publish a card count that TPCi has not announced. Set trackers
extrapolate those from the Japanese list and they are frequently wrong.
WHEN AN OFFICIAL PAGE AND A NEWS SITE DISAGREE ON A NUMBER, the official
one wins and the other is not printed beside it as an alternative.
pokemon.com says Delta Reign has 'more than 20 Trainer cards' and PokeBeach
says 'more than a dozen'. This file prints more than 20 and does not mention
the dozen at all, because printing both reads as a range nobody stated.
A NEWS SITE'S ANALYSIS IS NOT A FACT AND DOES NOT GO IN A HIGHLIGHT.
PokeBeach works out which Japanese sets Delta Reign is probably built from,
and hedges every sentence of it with 'should'. None of it is on the page.
What a source SAW (a product render, an announced date) is reportable; what
a source RECKONS is not, however well reasoned.
When something ships, delete it from here; the page filters past dates out
anyway, but the file should not grow forever.
NO PACK ODDS IN A HIGHLIGHT, however Pokemon words it. This file shipped
'30 different Pikachu illustrations by 30 illustrators, one guaranteed in
every pack' for 30th Celebration, which tells a reader how often one of a
30 card chase subset comes out of a pack. The site never states that in any
phrasing, and 'guaranteed' is exactly the wording somebody will argue is a
contents fact rather than a rate. What a pack HOLDS is fine and stays: the
next line, 'Packs are 5 foil cards plus a foil basic Energy', is a count of
what is in the wrapper and says nothing about which cards. pokemon.com's own
showcase still words it the forbidden way, and so does PokeGuardian, so the
wording will be offered back to this file every time somebody re-reads a
source. Keep the stripped form.
JAPANESE SETS ARE NOT ENGLISH SETS, and a reader must never be able to
mistake one date for the other. THAT is what this rule protects, so the rule
is about WHERE a Japanese date goes and not about whether it may be here at
all. It used to read 'Do not put a Japanese date on this page', and it was
rewritten rather than deleted on August 21, 2026 when the owner asked for the
Japanese calendar, because he collects Japanese cards and they land months
before the English ones. A rule that is quietly dropped is how the next pass
reintroduces the bug it was written to prevent.
So: NEVER put a Japanese date in `sets` or `products`. Those two are the
ENGLISH lists, an English reader reads every date in them as an English date,
and one Japanese row mixed in is exactly the confusion this rule exists to
stop. Japanese releases go in `japan.releases` and nowhere else. The builder
renders that as its own section, under its own heading, with its own lede
saying in plain words that these are Japan-only dates and are not the English
release. If you ever find yourself wanting one Japanese row in the English
list because it is 'related', that is the bug, and the answer is a sentence
in the English entry's blurb naming the Japanese set, not a row.

sets.name: Mega Evolution: Delta Reign
sets.blurb: The sixth English Mega Evolution set, headlined by Mega Rayquaza ex coming back to the card game. The Pokemon Company has published the whole card breakdown for this one, which is unusual this far out, and it comes with a new kind of Stadium card that only does anything as a pair.
highlights: Over 135 cards, more than 20 of them Trainer cards, and over 35 cards with special illustrations
Four new Mega Evolution Pokemon ex: Mega Rayquaza ex, Mega Golurk ex, Mega Malamar ex and Mega Golisopod ex

Split Stadium cards with Legendary in the name. Both halves carry the same name and you need both to play it, so a deck can hold two complete ones at most. Placed side by side they form one extended picture, and a pack holding one holds both of its halves

The rest of the breakdown, published by The Pokemon Company itself on August 20, 2026: six Stadium cards making three Legendary Stadiums, six Pokemon ex, 14 illustration rares, 17 ultra rares and six special illustration rares
Prereleases start October 24 at participating local game stores, which is The Pokemon Company's own date. It has not announced an end, so the November 1 finish is PokeBeach's
Pokemon TCG Live gets the set on November 5, the day before it reaches shelves

products.name: Booster Box
products.note: Four pack wraps: Mega Rayquaza, Mega Golisopod, Mega Golurk and Mega Malamar

products.name: Elite Trainer Box
products.note: The box promo is the Kyogre illustration rare from Japan's Storm Emeralda, cut from the English set and moved here

products.name: Pokemon Center Elite Trainer Box
products.note: Pokemon Center exclusive. A stamped version of the Kyogre promo has been shown as well

products.name: Premium Checklane Blister, Ampharos or Delphox
Target Checklane Blister, Xerneas and Deoxys or Keldeo and Delibird

sets.productNote: Every product here has been shown in official artwork, published by PokeBeach on August 20, 2026, so this is a real lineup rather than a guess at one. The Pokemon Company has still not put out a product page for the set, which is why not one of these carries a price or a date of its own here: none has been announced. If a shop quotes you a price for one, that is the shop's number and not a retail price. TCGPLAYER ADDITIONALLY LISTS THREE THAT TPCi HAS NOT SHOWN, and they are named here rather than added to the list above because the distinction is the whole point of that first sentence: a single Booster Pack, a Sleeved Booster Pack and a Half Booster Box, read off its "ME06: Delta Reign" listings on September 16, 2026, which carry 21 entries once distributor cases are set aside. A retailer listing is the `expected` standing this file's readme warns about -- "templated from the last set, not sourced" -- and every previous Mega Evolution set has all three, which is exactly what makes them unremarkable to template. Its listings also hold no card numbers yet, so there is still no English card list for this set anywhere.

products.name: Enhanced 2 Pack Blister
products.blurb: Gengar, Marshadow or Team Rocket's Mimikyu in cosmos holo, plus a metallic coin.

products.name: Mini Portfolio
products.blurb: Mega Greninja and Mega Zeraora on the front, Mega Darkrai and Mega Chandelure on the back. Comes with one Pitch Black pack.

products.name: Deck Crafter's Collection
products.blurb: The replacement for the Trainer's Toolkit. A foil Meowth ex, 39 tournament ready Trainer cards, dividers and one Pitch Black pack.

_note: JAPAN ONLY. Every date in here is a Japanese release date and none of them
is the English one. Read the Japanese rule in _readme above before adding
anything: the whole reason this list is a separate key, rendered as a
separate labeled section, is so that no reader can take one of these dates
for an English street date.
Same three confidence words as everything else. These are dates The Pokemon
Company has announced in Japan, read through PokeBeach, which is the same
standing this file already gives the PokeBeach-sourced rows in `products`.
Prices are in yen and are written with a yen sign so they cannot be read as
dollars. There is no dollar conversion here on purpose: it would be a rate
on the day somebody typed it and wrong by the time anybody read it.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT. Storm Emeralda and the three MEGA Starter
Set ex Decks both came out on July 31, 2026 and are already out, so they are
not upcoming and are not here; Storm Emeralda is named in Delta Reign's own
entry instead, which is where an English reader has a reason to care about
it. Taiwan, Hong Kong and Korean dates were looked at and dropped: this is a
Japanese calendar because that is what the owner asked for and what he buys, and a
section called Japan that quietly holds three other regions is the same
class of mistake as a Japanese date in the English list.

releases.name: Nine 30th Celebration Card Sets
releases.blurb: The 27 starter Pokemon promos that English speakers got in the First Partner Collections, split across nine card sets.

releases.name: Special Deck Set, Mega Feraligatr ex, Mega Dragonite ex and Mega Gengar ex
releases.blurb: Three decks in one box. English collectors already have alternate art Mega Feraligatr ex and Mega Gengar ex from the Ascended Heroes box and the Mega Moonlight tins.

releases.name: Aura Seeker
releases.blurb: Starring Mega Lucario Z ex. No English set has been named for it, and this page will not guess one: Japanese sets do not map one to one onto English ones, which Delta Reign above is the current proof of. Pokemon has now shown Riolu, Mega Lucario Z ex and Sigilyph ex from it, and the set itself is still not officially revealed. The English cards were teased at the same time carrying a set symbol named FLO, which is a symbol and not a name: it still does not say what the English set will be called, and this page will not turn a three letter symbol into one.

_note: NAMED BUT NOT DATED. Things The Pokemon Company has named or shown and given
no release date to -- not a day, not a month, not a quarter. They are not in
`sets` because that list is dated English sets and every row on it renders a
date and a countdown; a dateless row there prints an empty line where the
most prominent fact goes. They are not in `japan.releases` either, because
that list is Japanese DATES and these have none.
SO THIS IS NOT A FOURTH CONFIDENCE WORD. The readme is explicit that there
are three and deliberately not four, and that a thing shown without a date
gets a sentence rather than a badge. This key is that sentence, given a
place to live so the answer to "what is after the next set" stops being
nothing. Rows here carry NO date field at all, which is what keeps the
Japanese rule satisfied: there is no date to mistake for an English one.
A ROW STILL NEEDS AN OFFICIAL NAME. The readme's first editing rule applies
here unchanged -- never add a set that has not been officially named, because
AI-written card sites invent them. `region` says which market, in words, on
every row, because one of these is Japan's and one is not.
WHEN A DATE IS ANNOUNCED, MOVE THE ROW. An English set with a date belongs in
`sets`; a Japanese date belongs in `japan.releases`. Nothing should sit here
once it can sit there.

items.name: Pokemon ex★
items.region: The next series, not a set
items.note: Pokemon has named the series that follows Mega Evolution: Pokemon ex★. Entei, Suicune and Raikou were teased alongside the name. That is everything announced -- no set in the series has been named, and no date, month or quarter has been given for any of it. The name implies a new Pokemon ex mechanic and nobody has said what it does.
items.why: IN `outlook` AND NOT IN `sets` BECAUSE IT IS A SERIES, NOT A SET. Mega Evolution is the series and Delta Reign is a set in it; putting a series name in a list of sets would read as a release a reader could buy. PokeBeach reckons the block could start in the spring and that is NOT printed anywhere here: the readme's rule is that what a source saw is reportable and what it reckons is not, and a guessed season on a page people read for dates is the worst place to break it.

items.name: MEGA x MEGA Parade
items.region: Japan, and no English set has been named for it
items.note: Japan's next High Class Pack set. Pokemon has teased Mega Attack Rares from it, the comic book style illustrations that English collectors last saw in Ascended Heroes, which was Japan's MEGA Dream ex High Class Pack. The set itself has not been officially revealed.
items.why: NO DATE ROW, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE DEMOTION. PokeBeach refers to it as February's set, which would be a `window` in `japan.releases`, and in the same breath says the set "hasn't been officially revealed yet". Those two cannot both be true of a date The Pokemon Company has announced, which is the standing that list requires, so it goes here with no date rather than there with a month this file cannot stand behind. Move it the day Pokemon reveals it.
